text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. This process often uses automated builds, which means the software is put together without manual work. As part of the build, the system runs tests to check that everything works correctly. These tests help in catching issues early, before they become bigger problems. Many teams use CI pipelines to organize these steps. A pipeline automatically builds the code, runs the tests, and reports the results. This way, developers can fix mistakes quickly and keep the project stable.
